question: Compare bagging and boosting according to the ML terminology reference.
answer: Bagging in ML terminology is about combining several models to reduce variance, as per [S1] and [S2]. Boosting, exemplified by Gradient Boosting in [S6], combines several models to reduce bias, as per [S1] and [S2] [S6]. shows Gradient Boosting achieving the highest F1 among fraud runs.

S5.title: Ml Notation Abbreviations
S5.text: OOB: out-of-bag. In a random forest each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample, and the rows left out of that sample are the out-of-bag rows; about 36.8% (1/e) of the rows are out-of-bag for each tree. They provide a free validation estimate. MAE: mean absolute error. RMSE: root mean squared error. SGD: stochastic gradient descent. k-NN: k-nearest neighbors. PR AUC: area under the precision-recall curve; preferred over ROC AUC for strongly imbalanced classes. i.i.d.: independent and identically distributed. precision: in classification, TP / (TP + FP). It is not the same as measurement precision in statistics. sample: in machine learning a sample usually means one row of data (one example). In statistics a sample is a subset of a population. bias: the error from wrong assumptions of a model. The bias term (intercept) of a linear model is a different thing.
